countries.name: India
countries.summary: India's higher-education system is overseen by the Ministry of Education and its statutory regulators - the University Grants Commission for universities and degrees, the All India Council for Technical Education for technical and management programmes, and the National Medical Commission for medical education. International applicants normally enter through an institution's own international-admissions office, through the government's Study in India portal, or through a centrally administered scheme such as DASA for engineering and architecture seats at NITs, IIITs and other centrally funded technical institutes. Entry rules differ by nationality, residency status, the prior qualification held and the discipline chosen.
countries.whyStudentsChooseIt: International applicants look at India for English-taught degrees across computing, engineering, management, design, sciences, law and health disciplines, and for a single national application route: the Ministry of Education's Study in India portal issues an SII ID and lets an applicant send one profile to several participating institutes. Government-funded study places also exist through Indian Council for Cultural Relations scholarship schemes, which are applied for through Indian diplomatic missions rather than directly to a university. What an individual applicant can access depends on citizenship, residency status, how the prior qualification is assessed for equivalence, and whether the programme is attached to a national entrance test.
countries.climate: Climate varies widely by region, from alpine Himalayan conditions in the north to tropical coastal and semi-arid zones further south, with a June-to-September monsoon across most of the country.
countries.metaTitle: Study in India: Guide for International Students
countries.metaDescription: Regulators, admission routes, entrance tests, student visa and FRRO rules that international applicants should verify before applying to an Indian university.

universities.name: Symbiosis International (Deemed University)
universities.summary: Symbiosis International (Deemed University) is a private multidisciplinary university in Pune, Maharashtra, established under Section 3 of the UGC Act, 1956. Its Pune institutes teach management, law, liberal arts, media and design in English to students from more than 85 countries, with admissions for every international category run centrally by the Symbiosis Centre for International Education.
universities.campusLifestyle: SIU runs six Pune campuses - Senapati Bapat Road, Lavale, Hinjewadi, Viman Nagar, Model Colony and Kirkee - alongside sites in Bengaluru, Noida, Nashik, Hyderabad, Nagpur and Dubai. SIBM Pune sits on the Lavale hilltop campus at Gram Lavale, Tal Mulshi, PIN 412115; Symbiosis Law School, Pune is at Rohan Mithila, Viman Nagar. The wider Symbiosis family hosts more than 40,000 Indian and international students drawn from over 85 countries. Nine faculties cover Law, Management, Computer Studies, Medical and Health Sciences, Media and Communication, Humanities and Social Sciences, Engineering, Design and Education, and a Symbiosis Centre for Health Care operates on campus.
universities.cityProfile: Pune is a university and technology city in western Maharashtra, roughly 150 km inland from Mumbai, and SIU's campuses are spread across it rather than concentrated on one site. The registered university address is Gram Lavale, Tal Mulshi, Pune 412115, on a hill campus outside the city; SCIE's admissions office is in central Pune at Symbiosis Vishwabhavan, Senapati Bapat Road, Pune 411004, and other institutes sit at Viman Nagar in the east, Model Colony and Kirkee to the north, and Hinjewadi to the west beside the city's main IT corridor. That spread matters practically: which campus a programme belongs to determines where an admitted student reports, where hostel places are allocated, and how long the daily commute runs. Foreigners' registration for Pune is administered through the Police Commissioner's Office, and SCIE publishes its rules and document lists for students who need to register or extend a visa.
universities.practicalExposure: Applied work is built into the programmes rather than bolted on. At Symbiosis School for Liberal Arts, students complete a two-month community outreach project with a written report and presentation, an internship in the declared major assessed by project report and viva, and either a dissertation or a research project plus a mandatory seminar paper written to publishable standard, supported by core courses in research methods. Symbiosis Institute of Design admits on portfolio and streams students into Communication Design, Industrial Design, Fashion Design or Fashion Communication. Symbiosis Law School, Pune builds its B.A. LL.B. (Honours) curriculum to Bar Council of India regulations, with practical legal training and a research component. The SIBM Pune MBA offers specialisations in Marketing, Human Resource, Finance, Operations and Supply Chain Management, and Data Analytics. Across the university, the Global Immersion Programme lets students take a semester abroad at a partner university, using a floating credit semester that removes the need to map course content exactly, with mutual credit recognition and, in some cases, tuition waivers; summer and winter schools of two to four weeks and overseas internships run alongside it. SIU also receives incoming exchange and free-moving students for one or two semesters, with credits transferable back to the home university.
universities.hostelOverview: Students admitted to a residential programme must live in the campus hostel, and most institutes also offer hostel places on non-residential programmes. SCIE states that accommodation is not guaranteed: it is allocated against vacancies, and the institute Director or Principal decides. Undergraduate hostels run at Viman Nagar, Vishwabhavan, Lavale Hill Base, Lavale Hill Top, Model Colony, Noida, Hyderabad and Nagpur; postgraduate hostels add Hinjewadi, Bengaluru and Nashik. For Foreign Nationals SIU publishes hostel charges of USD 650 per year plus a USD 250 deposit. Hostel, mess and uniform fees fall outside the annual academic fee and are settled at the institute after the joining letter is submitted.
universities.dietarySupport: SIU publishes an annual meal plan for Foreign National students at USD 560 per year, charged separately from the academic fee and paid to the institute at joining alongside hostel and uniform charges. Catering is run by the individual institute rather than centrally, so menus and dietary arrangements are set campus by campus. SCIE runs cultural food programming through the year, including an international food festival during International Students' Day and an Iftar dinner for the student community.
universities.safetyOverview: Anti-ragging undertakings signed by both student and parent are compulsory at reporting, and SIU runs an anti-ragging cell alongside a Student Grievance Redressal Committee and an Ombudsperson. Every international student takes a medical examination at the Symbiosis Centre for Health Care on campus. SCIE publishes the Pune Police Commissioner's registration rules, including the 14-day FRRO deadline for long-term student visas.
universities.studentSupport: SCIE is the nodal department for international students from admission to graduation. It runs an orientation covering university rules, legal procedures and medical facilities, assigns buddies and mentors, helps set academic timetables, assists with finding accommodation and supports Foreigners' Registration Office formalities. An International Students' Council represents students, and International Students' Day falls on 29 to 31 July 2026.
whyChoose: One central channel handles everything: SCIE processes applications for every constituent institute, so a single application can reach management, law, liberal arts, media or design programmes.

Foreign National, OCI and PIO applicants are exempted from SIU's SET, SITEEE and SNAP entrance tests; shortlisting weighs transcripts at 90 per cent, the statement of purpose at 5 per cent and two recommendations at 5 per cent.

The Golden Jubilee Scholarship for Foreign Nationals covers academic fees at USD 1,300 a year for undergraduate programmes, USD 2,600 for MBA programmes and USD 1,950 for other postgraduate programmes.
SIU is a UGC deemed-to-be university with UGC Category-I status and NAAC A++ re-accreditation, ranked 24th in the NIRF 2025 university category.
Individual institutes rank in their own right: Symbiosis Law School, Pune placed 7th in the NIRF 2025 law category and SIBM Pune 11th in management.
Applicants can apply while awaiting Class 12 results using a principal-endorsed predicted score, and travel to India only after accepting an offer.
thingsToConsider: NRI, OCI and PIO applicants pay far more than Foreign Nationals: the 2026-27 SIBM Pune MBA academic fee is USD 23,200 a year for NRI and OCI against USD 2,600 for Foreign Nationals.
An Indian student visa does not permit employment or business activity, so no part-time earnings can be built into a funding plan.
IELTS Academic at 6.0 or the Symbiosis IELA test at band 4 is compulsory for Foreign National, OCI and PIO applicants, and the IELA sitting costs a further USD 50.
Eligibility documents not handed over at reporting must reach SCIE by 31 August; a student who misses that date cannot sit the Semester I examination and may forfeit the academic fee.
Fees for the SCMC Pune mass communication and SID Pune design programmes are still published for 2025-26, and the SCMC table is headed with the name of a different degree.

Symbiosis Law School Pune holds Bar Council of India approval to 2026-27, which governs practice in India; an Indian law degree does not by itself confer the right to practise in another jurisdiction.

faq.question: Is Symbiosis International a public or a private university?
faq.answer: It is a private university. Symbiosis International (Deemed University) is a deemed-to-be university established under Section 3 of the UGC Act, 1956, sponsored by the Symbiosis Society. It holds Category-I status from the UGC and is accredited by NAAC at Grade A++ with a CGPA of 3.56 in Cycle 3, declared in December 2022.

faq.question: How do international students apply, and is it different from the Indian route?
faq.answer: Yes, it is a separate channel. Admissions for Foreign Nationals, NRI, OCI and PIO applicants are centralised for every constituent institute through the Symbiosis Centre for International Education (SCIE) at scie.ac.in, not through the institute directly. Application, document upload, payment and admission-status tracking are all handled online, and the applicant travels to India only after accepting an offer.

faq.question: Do I have to sit SET, SITEEE or SNAP?
faq.answer: Foreign National, OCI and PIO candidates are exempted from SIU's entrance tests and instead take an English proficiency test. For NRI candidates applying under the international category, the entrance exam is not mandatory. Selection is made on academic transcripts weighted at 90 per cent, the statement of purpose at 5 per cent and two letters of recommendation at 5 per cent.

faq.question: What English test does Symbiosis accept?
faq.answer: An English proficiency test is compulsory for Foreign National, OCI and PIO applicants. Either IELTS Academic with a minimum overall score of 6.0, or Symbiosis's own International English Language Assessment (IELA), conducted online by the English Language Teaching Institute of Symbiosis, with a minimum band 4 out of 6. IELA is registered through the SCIE application form and costs USD 50. NRI applicants are not asked for an English test.

faq.question: How many seats are open to international applicants?
faq.answer: SCIE earmarks 20 per cent of the total intake of each programme for the international categories, which cover Foreign Nationals, PIO card holders, OCI card holders and Non-Resident Indians. Seats are therefore capped per programme rather than open-ended, and admission is on a merit list.

faq.question: Why are the fees so different for Foreign Nationals and for NRI or OCI applicants?
faq.answer: SIU publishes two separate fee tables for each programme. For the 2026-27 SIBM Pune MBA the Foreign National academic fee is USD 2,600 a year against USD 23,200 for NRI and OCI candidates. Undergraduate law at SLS Pune is USD 1,300 a year for Foreign Nationals and USD 8,900 for NRI and OCI. SIU's Golden Jubilee Scholarship covers academic fees for Foreign Nationals only, at USD 1,300 a year for undergraduate programmes, USD 2,600 for MBA programmes and USD 1,950 for other postgraduate programmes; it excludes Indian, NRI, OCI and PIO students, short-term programmes, doctoral programmes and part-time programmes.

faq.question: What does the full first-year cost look like beyond tuition?
faq.answer: Foreign Nationals pay a one-time application fee of USD 65, a one-time administrative fee of USD 275, a refundable institute deposit of USD 275 and, where applicable, USD 50 for the IELA test. Hostel accommodation is published at USD 650 per year plus a USD 250 deposit, and the annual meal plan at USD 560. Hostel, mess and uniform charges sit outside the annual academic fee and are settled at the institute on joining. NRI, OCI and PIO applicants pay USD 120 as the application fee and USD 550 as the administrative fee.

faq.question: Is accommodation guaranteed?
faq.answer: No. Students admitted to a residential programme must live in the campus hostel, and most institutes also offer hostel places to students on non-residential programmes, but SCIE states plainly that hostel accommodation is not guaranteed and is allocated against vacancies at the discretion of the institute Director or Principal. Undergraduate hostels operate at Viman Nagar, Vishwabhavan, Lavale Hill Base, Lavale Hill Top, Model Colony, Noida, Hyderabad and Nagpur.

faq.question: When are the 2026 intakes and reporting dates?
faq.answer: They vary by institute. SIBM Pune reports 29 May to 3 June 2026 with the MBA commencing 3 June. Symbiosis Law School Pune reports 24 to 27 June and 29 to 30 June, commencing in the first week of July. Symbiosis Institute of Design reports 29 and 30 June, commencing 1 July. Symbiosis Centre for Media and Communication reports 13 to 15 July, commencing 16 July. Symbiosis School for Liberal Arts reports 17 and 18 July, commencing 20 July 2026.

faq.question: Can I apply before my Class 12 results are out?
faq.answer: Yes, for undergraduate programmes. An applicant may submit a predicted score or pre-board marks endorsed by the school principal on school letterhead, together with the Class 12 hall ticket. The final board result must be uploaded as soon as it is declared, otherwise the application is not considered for the merit list. Nepali nationals submit the Class 11 final marksheet and pre-board marksheet instead.

faq.question: What happens after I arrive in Pune?
faq.answer: Reporting formalities include a medical examination at the Symbiosis Centre for Health Care on campus, confirmation of fee details with the accounts department and payment of any balance, and eligibility clearance. Anti-ragging and indemnification undertakings are signed by both student and parent, and the SIU eligibility form is executed on 500-rupee stamp paper. Any documents not produced at reporting must reach SCIE by 31 August, or the student is not permitted to sit the Semester I examination and may forfeit the academic fee.

faq.question: What are the visa and registration rules?
faq.answer: SCIE issues a Provisional Admission Letter for the visa application once the administrative fee and part payment of the annual academic fee are received. The visa must be a student visa naming Symbiosis International University; any other visa type is invalid for final admission. Foreign nationals on a visa longer than 180 days must register with the FRRO or FRO within 14 days of arrival, with shorter deadlines for Pakistani, Afghan and Bangladeshi nationals. Nepali and Bhutanese nationals are not asked for a visa or residential permit.

faq.question: Can I work part-time in India while studying?
faq.answer: No. The Bureau of Immigration states that students on an Indian student visa must not undertake employment or business activity in India, and must open a Non-Resident Ordinary bank account and give the details to the FRRO. Any funding plan therefore has to cover tuition and living costs without local earnings.

evidence.claimText: The University Grants Commission is the statutory body of the Government of India for coordination, determination and maintenance of standards of higher education, operating under the Ministry of Education.
evidence.internalNotes: UGC publishes the authoritative lists of Central, State, Deemed-to-be and State Private universities, plus a published list of fake universities. Corroborated by the Study in India portal Indian Higher Education page, which states all institutions are governed by the Ministry of Education.

evidence.claimText: The All India Council for Technical Education is the Government of India statutory body for technical education, covering engineering, management and allied technical programmes.
evidence.sourceLabel: All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE) - official site

evidence.claimText: The National Medical Commission is the Government of India regulator for medical education and medical institutions; medical and dental admission is governed separately from general higher education.
India's higher-education landscape includes over 1,100 universities and more than 45,000 colleges, all governed by the Ministry of Education, and higher education begins after 12 years of schooling.
evidence.sourceLabel: Study in India (Ministry of Education) - Indian Higher Education
evidence.internalNotes: Portal-published counts are approximate and shift between AISHE cycles; treat them as indicative and re-check at review. Regulator identity is separately verified against UGC and AICTE.

evidence.claimText: The Study in India portal is the Government of India route for international applicants: the applicant registers for a compulsory SII ID, explores participating institutes and courses, submits applications to several institutes from one profile, accepts an offer letter, then applies for a student visa or student e-visa.
evidence.sourceLabel: Study in India (Ministry of Education) - official portal

evidence.claimText: The Bureau of Immigration directs foreign nationals who wish to apply to Indian institutes to register under the Study in India scheme, confirming the portal as a government-recognised route rather than a third-party service.
evidence.sourceLabel: Bureau of Immigration, Ministry of Home Affairs - Study in India

evidence.claimText: The Indian Council for Cultural Relations administers Government of India scholarship schemes for international students at UG, PG and PhD level, including AYUSH streams; applications are handled through the ICCR A2A scholarship portal and the applicant's Indian diplomatic mission.
evidence.sourceLabel: ICCR Admissions to Alumni (A2A) Scholarship Portal
evidence.internalNotes: Portal states that applicants should contact the Indian Mission for scholarship updates - eligibility and open cycles are mission-specific and vary by country, so no scheme may be presented as open to all nationalities.

evidence.claimText: Foreign nationals must obtain a Student Visa to pursue on-campus, full-time structured courses or research at educational institutions recognised by the Government of India. Student (S-3) visas cover yoga, Vedic culture, Indian dance, music and Buddhist studies at approved institutions; Student (S-5) visas cover internships.
evidence.sourceLabel: Bureau of Immigration, Ministry of Home Affairs - Study in India

evidence.claimText: Foreign nationals entering India on a Student visa valid for more than 180 days must register with the jurisdictional FRRO or FRO within 14 days of arrival. Pakistani nationals must register within 24 hours. Children under 12 years and OCI cardholders are exempt from registration, and citizens of Nepal and Bhutan are exempt from both visa and registration requirements.
evidence.sourceLabel: Bureau of Immigration, Ministry of Home Affairs - Registration Requirements
evidence.internalNotes: Corroborated by the Study in India Onboarding & FRRO page, which states e-FRRO registration within 14 days of landing. Nationality-dependent rule - never state one universal deadline.

evidence.claimText: Students on an Indian Student visa must not undertake employment or business activity in India, must open a Non-Resident Ordinary (NRO) account with a recognised Indian bank and furnish the details to the FRRO, and must not enrol in off-campus franchise centres, distance-learning study centres of open universities or outreach programmes.
evidence.sourceLabel: Bureau of Immigration, Ministry of Home Affairs - Study in India
evidence.internalNotes: Directly constrains any work-rights or earn-while-you-study claim on India pages. Do not publish part-time work guidance for India.

evidence.claimText: An applicant should possess proof of admission to a full-time regular academic course at a recognised Indian institution and evidence of financial support, and must also hold a No Objection Certificate from the Ministry of Health where the admission is to a medical or paramedical course.
evidence.sourceLabel: Study in India (Ministry of Education) - Onboarding & FRRO
evidence.internalNotes: The portal adds its own disclaimer that document requirements differ across countries and must be confirmed with the nearest Indian embassy.

evidence.claimText: Admission for Foreign Nationals, OCIs, PIOs and NRIs to undergraduate engineering, architecture and planning programmes at NITs, IIEST, IIITs, SPAs and other centrally funded technical institutes runs through the Ministry of Education DASA scheme, and for the 2026-27 year admission is on the basis of JEE (Main) 2026. DASA seats are supernumerary and capped at up to 15 per cent of a programme's total seats. IITs are outside the DASA scheme.
evidence.sourceLabel: Information Brochure DASA 2026 (UG), Central Seat Allocation Board / Ministry of Education
evidence.internalNotes: The qualifying-exam basis has changed between cycles (SAT in earlier cycles, JEE Main for 2026-27). Never state the accepted exam without naming the admission year. Corroborated by dasanit.org, which describes DASA as an MoE scheme for Foreign Nationals, PIOs, OCIs and NRIs to NITs, CFTIs and other premier technical institutions other than IITs.

evidence.claimText: Non-Resident Indians, Overseas Citizens of India and Foreign Nationals are eligible to appear in NEET (UG) and are eligible for admission to medical and dental colleges subject to the rules of the respective State Governments, institutions and the Government of India. Foreign applicants must upload documentary proof of nationality with the application and are directed to confirm eligibility with the competent state and counselling authorities.
evidence.sourceLabel: Information Bulletin NEET (UG)-2026, National Testing Agency
evidence.internalNotes: Chapter 6, sections 1-2. No India medical page may present a NEET-free route. Eligibility is explicitly conditional on state and institution rules, so it varies by college.

evidence.claimText: The National Assessment and Accreditation Council, established in 1994 as an autonomous institution of the UGC, assesses and accredits Indian higher education institutions. The National Institutional Ranking Framework, launched by the Ministry of Education in September 2015, is the government ranking framework for Indian institutions.
evidence.internalNotes: NIRF corroborated separately at https://www.nirfindia.org/Home (MoE, launched 29 September 2015). Use a NAAC grade or NIRF rank only with the assessment or ranking year stated.

evidence.claimText: The UGC publishes a list of fake universities alongside its lists of Central, State, Deemed-to-be and State Private universities, so institutional recognition must be checked against UGC records before an Indian institution is presented as degree-awarding.
evidence.sourceLabel: University Grants Commission - Higher Education Institutions listings
evidence.internalNotes: Operational rule for this catalogue: no Indian university is published without a verifiable UGC listing and, where applicable, AICTE approval or NMC recognition.

evidence.claimText: India spans Himalayan, tropical coastal, semi-arid and monsoon-affected climate zones, with the southwest monsoon typically running from June to September.
evidence.sourceLabel: India Meteorological Department, Ministry of Earth Sciences
evidence.internalNotes: General climatic framing only; do not present city-level weather claims at country level.

evidence.claimText: Symbiosis International (Deemed University) is established under Section 3 of the UGC Act, 1956 and awarded Category-I status by the UGC; its registered address is Lavale, Pune 412115, Maharashtra.
NAAC records Symbiosis International (Deemed University), AISHE U-0329, Maharashtra, at Grade A++ with a CGPA of 3.56 in Cycle 3, declared 20 December 2022.

evidence.internalNotes: Regulator verification 2026-08-22 by claude-india-regverify-20260822, corroborated against 136th Standing Committee result PDF (136SC_Appeal.pdf, 20 Dec 2022). The workbook publishes a declaration date, not an expiry date, so no validity end date is stated in public copy.

evidence.claimText: The Bar Council of India Approved List of Centres of Legal Education records Symbiosis Society's Law College, Pune with approval to 2026-27 for its 5-year B.A. LL.B. (Hons.), 5-year BBA LL.B. (Hons.), 5-year B.Com. LL.B. (Hons.) and 3-year LL.B. courses.

BCI approval attaches to UG law courses only; no LL.M. claim is made because BCI does not accredit LL.M. programmes.

evidence.claimText: The NBA Management (Post Graduate) register lists Symbiosis Institute of Business Management Pune, Symbiosis International (Deemed University), programme Master of Business Administration, level Post Graduate, status ACCREDITED, for academic years 2024-25, 2025-26 and 2026-27, upto 30 June 2027.

evidence.internalNotes: Regulator verification 2026-08-22 by claude-india-regverify-20260822; register row re-read directly from the NBA Management (Post Graduate) register on 2026-08-22. NBA Management (Post Graduate) register row, read 2026-08-22: 'Symbiosis Institute of Business Management Pune, Symbiosis International (Deemed University) (Pune) | Master of Business Administration | Post Graduate | ACCREDITED | Academic Year 2024-25, 2025-26 and 2026-27, i.e., upto 30/06/2027'. The register names this exact programme, so the badge is scoped to it rather than to 'MBA (various)'. Sibling SIU institutes hold separately named awards (SIIB Pune MBA (International Business), SIOM Nashik MBA (Operations Management)) and are not covered by this badge. Only the accreditation period evidences current status. SIU's Tier I (Washington Accord) engineering holdings sit with Symbiosis Institute of Technology, whose B.Tech programmes are not packaged in this bundle, so no Tier I badge is written here. SIU is not on the UGC Institution of Eminence list and no IoE claim is made.
